abstract: kALDo 2.3.0 adds a dedicated non-analytic correction engine, anharmonic free-energy corrections from the cumulant expansion, and memory checks for parallel force constants. It also rebuilds IFC interpolation, which changes some results, and fixes two bugs that affected force constants in 2.2.x. New features The non-analytic correction (NAC) has a dedicated engine that uses the Quantum ESPRESSO rigid-ion convention for q2r input and the phonopy (Gonze-Lee) convention otherwise. It turns on when the atoms carry a dielectric tensor and nonzero (n_atoms, 3, 3) Born charges. The new is_nac=False turns it off, and nac_q_direction sets the direction of approach to Gamma. Active NAC requires a diagonal supercell and rejects distance_threshold ( #307 ). kaldo.cumulant computes anharmonic free-energy corrections from the phonon cumulant expansion ( F1_from_fc , F2_from_fc , cumulant_thermo ) ( #283 ). Parallel force-constant calculations check available memory first. With n_workers=None , kALDo uses the smaller of the CPU count and the memory-safe limit (2.2.x used all CPUs); an explicit n_workers above the limit raises MemoryError . KALDO_MEMORY_HEADROOM sets the fraction of available memory kept free (default 0.05). The estimate covers host memory only, so pass GPU calculators as a factory ( #248 , #321 ). The documentation now covers installation with uv ( #300 ) and has user guides for IFC interpolation and the non-analytic correction ( #308 ). Changes that affect results IFC interpolation no longer depends on where the unit-cell origin is drawn ( #306 ). For systems periodic in all three directions, both the default is_unfolding=False and is_unfolding=True use the shortest Wigner-Seitz images of each atom pair; TDEP and QE d3q third-order data keep their own convention.…

summary.how: NAC uses the Quantum ESPRESSO rigid-ion convention for q2r input and the phonopy (Gonze-Lee) convention otherwise; it turns on when atoms carry a dielectric tensor and Born charges, and requires a diagonal supercell. IFC interpolation changes may alter some results. With n_workers=None the code uses the smaller of the CPU count and a memory-safe limit.
summary.impact: Directly relevant to the GaN/AlGaN HEMT, InGaAs and boron arsenide projects: kALDo is a phonon BTE code that works alongside phonopy/phono3py, and NAC matters for polar materials such as GaN and AlGaN. Worth checking whether the IFC interpolation change or the 2.2.x force-constant bugs affect any existing results, and whether the cumulant free-energy tools are useful for anharmonic work.
summary.what: kALDo 2.3.0 adds a dedicated non-analytic correction (NAC) engine and anharmonic free-energy corrections from the phonon cumulant expansion (kaldo.cumulant). It also adds memory checks for parallel force-constant calculations.
summary.why: Release notes state it fixes two bugs that affected force constants in 2.2.x and rebuilds IFC interpolation so it no longer depends on where the unit-cell origin is drawn.
